A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 39-page versions of the same Conductor study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original Conductor training and evaluation results, baseline comparisons, ablations, and recursive-scaling experiments in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v5 retains the same original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including controlled comparisons and ablation experiments.

M1.justification: The GRPO training procedure, workflow specification and execution, adaptive worker selection, and recursive extension remain unchanged in Sections 2–3 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged across the math, coding, and general/scientific reasoning benchmarks. Appendix E also retains the same Medreason, DeepMath, and Countdown few-shot sources.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain identical comparator sets, including individual workers, self-reflection and consensus baselines, MASRouter, MoA, RouterDC, both Smoothie variants, and GPT-5/Gemini conductor replacements.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same splits, model sizes, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and constrained versus unconstrained protocols. No experimental setting is reported as revised.

E4.justification: The model-scale, subtask, agent-selection, few-shot, and topology analyses are unchanged, as are the efficiency and recursion analyses and Appendix F completion case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report repeating evaluations up to 16 times depending on task size and reporting mean accuracy and standard errors. Repeated-sampling details and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports Conductor scores of 83.93 on LiveCodeBench and 87.5 on GPQA-Diamond in both versions.

T1.justification: The workflow definition and GRPO objective and advantage equations (1)–(2) are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution bullets, and scientific conclusions retain the same claims about learned orchestration, benchmark performance, customizable worker pools, and recursive test-time scaling.

C2.justification: Interpretations of agent complementarity, prompt engineering, OOD few-shot conditioning, and recursive adaptation remain unchanged. The economic-access concern and proposed multimodal extensions are also retained.

D1.justification: v5 removes code-sharing statements from the introduction and Section 6 and deletes the reproducibility statement's disclosure of supplementary source code and trained weights in an anonymized repository. Implementation details and prompts in Appendices A/E remain unchanged. The PDFs establish removal of this disclosure, without establishing actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is Section 5's positioning against tool-using RL, model routing, and manually designed multi-agent coordination.

P1.justification: A few sentences are deleted or rewritten in the introduction, Section 6, and reproducibility statement, and the arXiv version/date marker changes. Section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and placement. The prose edits cause limited local text and whitespace reflow on pages 2, 10, and 11; the remaining presentation is unchanged apart from the version/date marker.

improvement.justification: v5 removes explicit code and trained-weight availability information without replacement access guidance, modestly weakening reproducibility documentation. The unchanged implementation details in Appendices A/E limit the impact, while the scientific evidence remains identical. This assessment concerns the documentation; the PDFs do not establish whether external resources were actually withdrawn.
